title: An artist vibe coded this in less than a week and I am impressed
author: Low-Cook-3544
selftext:
I've seen many quickly vibe coded games but nothing like this. The character art, motion, sound effects, and little engagement nuggets are so much more impressive than most vibe coded games and they clearly show the artist's taste and attention to detail. 

  
The most beautiful part is all the bits of Filipino culture sprinkled into the gameplay. What do you think of it?

comments.author: Statcat2017
comments.body: It looks absolute ass to play.

replies.author: ArtArtArt123456
replies.body:
the low framerate sections look terrible. genuinely uncomfortable.

the whole thing does have a bit of polish, but not enough really. there is no soundtrack for example. and the gameplay looks janky as hell.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: Yeah I don't know how anyone plays more than a couple minutes of this before being over it

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body:
AI doesn't make someone a gamedev.

It's like holding a paintbrush doesn't make you an artist. Sure you can slam paint on a canvas but why? What's the message, the idea, the goal?

Same with this game. It's missing.. the game.

replies.author: Low-Cook-3544
replies.body: I see your point, it's not a full game even if there are powerups and stuff. Even if it is a mobile game. I actually found it touching though because the creator talks about his Lola in the game description and the culture that raised him. I thought it was a fun use case of someone new to game dev who looked around their environment and thought "Hey, I can make a game about that!" and for a first try given how low quality AI vibe coding tools are I think it's pretty damn impressive.

comments.author: Kolaps_
comments.body:
The artist?   
Why every time there is an A.I. stuff, technophiles need to add "artist".  Do you use this word as often as you talk of any creative activity?

Let's judge this in comparison of the actual video game market state. This is shitty. Having the first 30% of your game's qualitiy is not the harder part, the harder part is the last 30%.

replies.author: Low-Cook-3544
replies.body: He's a self-disclosed artist traditional/digital/toy artist lol I didn't make this up. It's a creative person trying out a new canvas. I've seen much worse 30%s of a game for a game jam and I'm genuinely surprised by the hate this is getting...

replies.author: Kolaps_
replies.body:
You are not answering my question.

Do you use the term “artist” for every creative activity as well? Or is it only systematic when it refers to an AI user?

I am not judging whether the person is an artist or not. To be honest, I find that question really stupid. I have worked with many people who could be considered artists: writers, musicians, illustrators, directors, game designers, and so on.

When you create something, it is extremely pompous to systematically talk about “art.” Artistic validation is not something you grant yourself. It is not self-awarded, and it cannot be the reason why you create, nor a justification of quality.

The debate around art and AI is sterile.

Then, the fact that some game jam games are bad does not make what you are sharing any more valuable. They're just shitty game made by ppl and shitty game made with A.I.

Here, the only qualities highlighted in your post are that it was made quickly and with AI. From a creative standpoint, and considering what video games actually are that has no value.

When Lotte Reiniger made her cut-out paper films, they were not interesting simply because they were made with cut-out paper. They were interesting because she injected cinematography into them, explored themes that were rare for her time, and knew how to take the qualities of her medium and production method and elevate them through expression and creation.

If we follow your logic, we should just look at video game production as a performance.

That is what I often criticize in “AI artists”: they are not interested in the field they claim to want to join. They are focused only on performance and speed of execution, without ever realizing that technicians and creators are far more meticulous in what they produce than what is usually shared on Reddit.

And I know what I am talking about. I worked for 15 years in audiovisual production and 8 years in video games, across different positions.

comments.author: OurPillowGuy
comments.body: The art style sucks. Looks super low effort, inconsistent, and kinda racist. Are you sure an artist made this?

replies.author: Low-Cook-3544
replies.body: I haven't seen their other art but it's how they introduce themselves. I've seen many ordinary 30-40 yr old dudes trying to make games though and they come out so much worse than this. It's certainly not a Steam-worthy game but for a small mobile game I think it's really good...
